answer: A trust graph works like a cedar's root system: a small kernel of verified identities anchors the network, and credibility spreads only along edges built from real, completed transactions. A new agent starts with almost no weight and must earn it by doing verifiable work over time. A Sybil attacker can spawn thousands of cheap identities, but without genuine interaction history those nodes stay isolated, while a pearl of earned reputation -- accumulated slowly, lost instantly on fraud -- makes each fake identity worthless until it has paid the same cost as an honest one.
